solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Singer with business in RAM, possibly diplomatic type

indicators.note: in places the singer and the business inside the rearranged ram
possibly says the letters of RAM may be arranged some other way

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
ado means fuss or business, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A singer with dealings at the Royal Academy of Music turns out to have a diplomat's manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make RAM look like the Royal Academy of Music, but 'possibly' makes it fodder, giving AMR, which 'in' wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy representing a state abroad is the archetypal diplomatic figure.

clue.text: More than one fool experiences losing power

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for experiences

parts.note: to pass through something is to experience it
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A fool repeatedly finds himself stripped of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys are proverbially stupid, so the plural names several silly people.

clue.text: Hurry into bar, picking up sort of refreshment?

indicators.note: into says the hurry goes inside the turned bar
picking up, in a down light, lifts the word for bar so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a pub is a bar
to rush is to hurry

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a pub hoping to collect a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'refreshment' looks like a drink, but it is refreshing one's knowledge, as in a quick revision.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick revision of a skill refreshes it; the question mark flags the unusual sense of refreshment.

clue.text: Assail economic works every so often in America

indicators.note: works, as in a reworking, tells us to rebuild the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A demand to attack economic policy, issued now and then in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An American term for something happening at irregular, fairly infrequent intervals.

clue.text: Serve fruit drink, not cold, but on time

indicators.note: on says the time letter follows on after the rest
not cold means the letter for cold is removed from the drink

parts.note: cassis is a blackcurrant drink or liqueur
C stands for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An instruction to serve a fruit cordial at room temperature, punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' looks like the waiter's verb of the surface, but it means help; 'not' drops the C and 'on' adds T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve someone is to help or aid them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Resident military leader's trophy given to soldier

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding, a military leader
a cup is a sporting trophy
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A commanding officer living locally hands his trophy to a private.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living in or holding a property is its occupier or dweller.

clue.text: Leader's error, putting Society first

indicators.note: putting, with first, tells us to shift one letter to the front
first says where the society letter is placed in the word for error

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to botch it, so a hash is an error

explanation.surface: A leader's blunder comes from putting high society before everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... first' moves the S of HASH to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian monarch was the ruler, or head, of the country.

clue.text: Atrocious German article suppressed by royal family mostly

indicators.note: suppressed by puts the article under, so inside, the royal house
mostly means all but the final letter of the dynasty word is kept

parts.note: a royal dynasty is called a house, as in the House of Windsor
ein is the German indefinite article, a or an

explanation.surface: A wicked German item is hushed up by most of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: A royal family is called a house, as in the House of Windsor; 'mostly' drops its last letter, and 'suppressed by' sets the article within.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe deeds that are utterly wicked and shocking.

clue.text: Dishonest wayward lotus-eaters

indicators.note: wayward suggests the letters of dishonest wander out of order

explanation.surface: Lazy pleasure-seekers described as crooked and unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: Lotus-eaters are, in Homer's Odyssey, people who live in dreamy indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus-eaters live only for idle pleasure, which is what pleasure-seekers devoted to enjoyment do.

clue.text: Proper border control left off getting upset about Australian, according to hearsay

indicators.note: about puts the remaining letters around the Australian letter

parts.note: U means proper or upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

indicators.note: getting upset says the letters are overturned and rearranged
off means the letter for left is taken away from the phrase

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that border control lost its temper about an Australian visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' drops L from BORDER CONTROL; U joins the rest and 'getting upset' rearranges them; 'about' wraps that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim based only on hearsay has no supporting evidence or confirmation.

clue.text: Columbus is at sea, ignoring black American tunes

indicators.note: at sea means muddled, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring says one letter of the explorer's name is left out

explanation.surface: Columbus, sailing the ocean, pays no attention to the black Americans' music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes the B (black, a pencil grade) from COLUMBUS; 'at sea' rearranges the rest with IS. The B does double duty, also in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of popular music from Black American gospel and rhythm and blues.

clue.text: Scotsman recalled poster's divine female figure

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, sends the name backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
an ad, or advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: A Scot remembers the goddess-like figure painted on a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph is a minor goddess of rivers and springs.

clue.text: Fish, slightly chilled, around front of hole on board

indicators.note: on, read with board as being aboard, puts the rest inside the vessel

parts.note: on board means aboard ship; a steamship is abbreviated SS

indicators.note: around puts the chill word round the front of hole

parts.note: cool is slightly cold, so slightly chilled

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of hole

explanation.surface: Fish lightly chilled around a hole on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like the noun of the surface, but it is a verb: the answer is what a trawler does in the water, and the definition is one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish swimming together in large groups are said to form shoals; as a verb it means to swim in such groups.

clue.text: Possibly he is to make declaration banning church

indicators.note: banning means the church letters are excluded from the verb

parts.note: to pronounce is to declare formally
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: He might declare something while barring the church.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one example of a word standing in for a noun, a grammatical part of speech.

clue.text: Content of argument closed with a snap

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
a pic is a photograph, a snap

explanation.surface: The argument ended with a sharp click, or with a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: The subject matter of a discussion or debate is what it is about.

clue.text: County supports suggestion for county officers

indicators.note: supports in a down light puts the county under, below the suggestion

parts.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion
Staffs is the short form of Staffordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A county backs a proposal for its own officials.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFS is Staffordshire, a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: These court officials once carried a metal-tipped staff as a badge of office.

clue.text: Delegates decline to appear amongst fellows Government sacked

indicators.note: to appear amongst places the decline word inside the fellows
sacked means the government letter is fired from the word

parts.note: gents are men, fellows
to rust is to decay or decline

explanation.surface: The government's dismissed, so decline sets in amongst the fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' takes G from GENTS, leaving ENTS for RUST to enter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over a task or responsibility to someone is to delegate it to them.

clue.text: Exclaim about a lake and marsh being taken over by insect

indicators.note: about puts the exclaim word round the remaining pieces

parts.note: to cry out is to exclaim

indicators.note: being taken over, read as turned over, flips lake and marsh

parts.note: a fen is a marsh

explanation.surface: Someone cries out as an insect swarms over a lake and its marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken over' turns L FEN into NEFL.
explanation.definitionFit: A daddy-long-legs is a long-legged fly, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Request certainly giving gratification

parts.note: a plea is a request
sure means certainly, as in a reply

explanation.surface: A request granted with a ready yes gives satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the feeling of satisfaction and enjoyment.

clue.text: What waiter will do, turning up with the French food

indicators.note: turning up in a down light reverses the waiting word

parts.note: one who waits will bide, wait
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A waiter arrives to serve the French dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The waiter is not a restaurant server but anyone who waits.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fit to be eaten are foodstuffs or provisions.

clue.text: More payment on boarding public transport

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so inside, the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle of public transport

explanation.surface: Bus passengers asked to pay more fare on boarding.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra sum paid on top of normal wages is additional payment.

clue.text: Hero, knocked over, retaining less than half strength, gets a breather

indicators.note: retaining means the hero holds the part of strength inside
knocked over in a down light turns the hero upside down

parts.note: a brave person is called a lion

indicators.note: less than half means the first three of the eight letters of strength

explanation.surface: A hero, felled and with his strength sapped, takes a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' gives NOIL, and 'retaining' puts STR, under half of STRENGTH, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is something one breathes through.

clue.text: Troops of great skill doing for threat

parts.note: men are soldiers, troops
ace means great expertise, as an ace player

explanation.surface: Highly skilled troops pose a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a danger or a source of possible harm.

clue.text: Hat's damaged, being filled with a good deal of grain

indicators.note: being filled with puts the grain inside the damaged word

parts.note: torn means ripped, damaged

indicators.note: a good deal of means most of the grain word, its end lopped

parts.note: rice is a grain

explanation.surface: A torn hat is stuffed with most of the rice.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-cornered hat of the eighteenth century is a type of headwear.

clue.text: American is about to regret backing large bloc of countries

indicators.note: backing means read the whole string from back to front

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: An American is about to wish she had not supported a large group of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass joining Europe and Asia contains many nations.

clue.text: Entrance halls: a test sees length cut

indicators.note: cut means the length letter is removed from the test

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: An entrance hall gets a trial that shortens its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Atriums, central halls at a building's entrance, take this Latin plural.

clue.text: Chap's first hill climbed?

parts.note: a fell is a hill, especially in northern England
A means first, as in grade A or A1

explanation.surface: A man's first conquest of a hill, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: FELL is the northern English word for a hill or moorland; 'climbed?' hints that it is a hill one climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal spelling of a word for a man or bloke.

clue.text: Coffee about to be brought in by friar, the sycophant

indicators.note: brought in by means the friar's letters hold the others

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Friar
a latte is a milky coffee
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A friar brings coffee to the toady.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning person who praises others insincerely to gain favour.

clue.text: Huge? Huge? On reflection, mediocre

indicators.note: on reflection, as in a mirror, means the letters are flipped round

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size meaning huge
a second OS for outsize

explanation.surface: Something touted as huge turns out, after thought, to be only average.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean only middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Unwisely upheld airy veneration of Madonna

indicators.note: unwisely suggests the letters are put together in an ill-judged order

explanation.surface: Holding up an airy ideal of the Virgin is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic theology the special veneration due to the Virgin Mary is given this technical name.
